topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a series of conflicts in fifteenth-century England between noble factions supporting rival claimants to the throne from the houses of Lancaster and York

examples.en-GB: The Wars of the Roses ended when Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth in 1485.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a line of rulers from the same family; Lancaster, York and Tudor were the main dynasties involved in the Wars of the Roses

examples.en-GB: Henry VII founded the Tudor dynasty after defeating Richard III, ending Yorkist rule.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the accepted right to rule; a king needed military power but also needed people to believe his rule was lawful and proper

examples.en-GB: Henry VII strengthened his legitimacy by marrying Elizabeth of York, uniting Lancastrian and Yorkist claims.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a group of people who work together for political power; in this period, factions often formed around powerful nobles or royal claimants

examples.en-GB: Noble factions competed for control of Henry VI's government, each trying to gain offices, land and the king's favour.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a person who served a noble in return for wages, protection, land or favour; retainers could form part of a noble's private armed force

examples.en-GB: Powerful nobles built up large numbers of retainers, who could be summoned as a private army in times of conflict.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a war between groups within the same country; the Wars of the Roses were civil wars because English nobles fought each other for control of the throne

examples.en-GB: Civil war made life dangerous for many ordinary people, who might be forced to support their local lord's side.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a person who argues that they have a right to a title or position, especially the throne

examples.en-GB: Both the Lancastrian and Yorkist sides had claimants to the throne who argued their family line gave them the right to rule.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: to take power from someone by force or without full legal agreement; opponents of Richard III accused him of usurping the throne from Edward V

examples.en-GB: Richard III was accused of usurping the throne from his nephew Edward V in 1483.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: information or images designed to persuade people to think in a particular way; Tudor propaganda portrayed Richard III as a villain to justify Henry VII's rule

examples.en-GB: Shakespeare's portrayal of Richard III as evil was shaped by Tudor propaganda and was not necessarily an accurate historical account.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the 1485 battle at which Henry Tudor defeated and killed Richard III, ending Yorkist rule and beginning the Tudor dynasty

examples.en-GB: The Battle of Bosworth was a turning point: Richard III was killed, and Henry VII became the first Tudor king.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the Lancastrian king who ruled England from 1422; his weak leadership, mental illness and failure in France contributed to the outbreak of the Wars of the Roses

examples.en-GB: Henry VI's mental illness in 1453 created a political crisis as nobles competed to control the government in his absence.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: Edward V and his brother Richard, who disappeared while held in the Tower of London in 1483; their fate remains a historical mystery

examples.en-GB: Historians still debate what happened to the Princes in the Tower because the evidence is limited and biased.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the Yorkist king from 1483 to 1485 who took power from his nephew Edward V; he was defeated and killed at Bosworth

examples.en-GB: Richard III's reputation has been shaped by Tudor propaganda, making it difficult to separate fact from bias when studying his reign.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the Lancastrian claimant who won the Battle of Bosworth in 1485, founded the Tudor dynasty and strengthened his rule through law, marriage and propaganda

examples.en-GB: Henry VII married Elizabeth of York in 1486 to unite the Lancastrian and Yorkist claims and give his dynasty greater legitimacy.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the 1461 battle at which the Yorkist Edward IV defeated Lancastrian forces, one of the largest and bloodiest battles fought on English soil

examples.en-GB: Edward IV's victory at Towton was decisive because it replaced the Lancastrian Henry VI with a Yorkist king.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: betrayal of the monarch or country; in the Wars of the Roses, defeated enemies could be accused of treason and punished accordingly

examples.en-GB: Henry VII dated his reign from the day before Bosworth so that those who had fought for Richard III could be accused of treason.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the queen of Henry VI who became a leading defender of Lancastrian interests, especially the right of her son to inherit the throne

examples.en-GB: Margaret of Anjou organised Lancastrian resistance against the Yorkists, showing the political role queens could play in medieval England.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: an event that causes an important change in a situation; the Battle of Bosworth was a turning point because it ended Yorkist rule and began the Tudor dynasty

examples.en-GB: Historians describe Bosworth as a turning point because Henry VII's victory changed England's ruling dynasty permanently.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a regent appointed to govern on behalf of a child king until they were old enough to rule; Richard Duke of Gloucester became Protector for Edward V in 1483

examples.en-GB: Rather than governing as Protector for young Edward V, Richard Duke of Gloucester took the throne himself as Richard III.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a view or explanation of the past; historians may create different interpretations because they use different evidence or ask different questions

examples.en-GB: Historians offer different interpretations of Richard III's character because the main sources were written under Tudor rule and may be biased.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the series of conflicts between England and France from 1337, during which England lost most of its French territory; this defeat weakened Henry VI's government

examples.en-GB: England's loss of French lands by 1453 damaged Henry VI's reputation and added pressure to the political tensions that led to the Wars of the Roses.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a member of the powerful upper class, such as a duke, earl or baron, who held large estates and wielded significant political and military power

examples.en-GB: Powerful nobles like the Earl of Warwick could shift the balance of power between Lancaster and York.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: an assembly that approved laws and taxes; during the Wars of the Roses, Parliament was used to support claims to the throne and declare enemies traitors

examples.en-GB: Henry VII used Parliament to legalise his rule and to declare those who had supported Richard III as traitors.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: the first Yorkist king, who came to power after victory at Towton in 1461 and ruled until his death in 1483, apart from a brief period of Lancastrian restoration in 1470

examples.en-GB: Edward IV was a strong military leader whose victories stabilised Yorkist rule, though his death in 1483 led to further instability.

topics: Late Medieval Conflict and the Wars of the Roses

data.targetWord: a reason why something happened; historians identify long-term, medium-term and short-term causes to explain why events like the Wars of the Roses occurred

examples.en-GB: The long-term cause of the Wars of the Roses included rival royal claims; the short-term cause included Henry VI's mental illness in 1453.

items: Wins the Battle of Bosworth and kills Richard III
Claims throne from the day before Bosworth to brand opponents as traitors
Marries Elizabeth of York to unite Lancaster and York
Uses Parliament to confirm his rule
Defeats the last Yorkist challenge at Stoke Field (1487)

England lost most French lands by 1453 (medium-term political damage)
Henry VI's weak rule and factional competition at court
Henry VI's mental illness in 1453 creates a power vacuum
Armed clashes at St Albans in 1455 make conflict unavoidable
